claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 1999

claims.claim: Caspase-processed HPK1 forms a 43 kD kinase domain-containing N-terminal fragment and a 54 kD C-terminal fragment containing three proline-rich regions and the citron homology domain.
claims.source: Caspase-processed HPK1 forms a 43 kD kinase domain-containing N-terminal fragment and a 54 kD C-terminal fragment containing three proline-rich regions and the citron homology domain (Chen et al., 1999).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 1999

claims.claim: The cleaved N-terminal kinase domain acquires a more hyperactive and sustained kinase activity than the non-cleaved full length HPK1 while retaining its ability to activate the JNK MAPK pathway.
claims.source: The cleaved N-terminal kinase domain acquires a more hyperactive and sustained kinase activity than the non-cleaved full length HPK1 while retaining its ability to activate the JNK MAPK pathway (Arnold et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Arnold et al., 2007

claims.claim: The kinase activity of HPK1 activates the JNK pathway via the activation of the MEKK1/MKK/JNK signaling cascade.
claims.source: The association between HPK1 kinase activity and the activation of JNK MAPK pathway had been previously established (Kiefer et al., 1996; Hu et al., 1996) and ectopic expression studies using dominant interfering mutants that function upstream of JNK in hematopoietic and epithelial cell lines revealed that the kinase activity of HPK1 activate the JNK pathway via the activation of the MEKK1/MKK/JNK signaling cascade (Hu et al., 1996; Chen and Tan, 2000).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Kiefer et al., 1996; Hu et al., 1996; Chen and Tan, 2000

claims.claim: The three-dimensional structure of HPK1 kinase domain exists as a head-to-head domain-swapped dimer in both the crystal form and in the liquid form.
claims.source: This speculation is strengthened by the recent X-ray crystallographic studies revealing that the three-dimensional structure of HPK1 kinase domain exists as a head-to-head domain-swapped dimer in both the crystal form, as well as in the liquid form Wu et al., 2019; Johnson et al., 2019.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Wu et al., 2019; Johnson et al., 2019

claims.claim: In the non-phosphorylated, inactive state, the activation loop of each HPK1 monomer partially occupies the ATP- and substrate-binding sites of its partner monomer.
claims.source: In the non-phosphorylated, inactive state, the activation loop of each HPK1 monomer partially occupies the ATP- and substrate-binding sites of its partner monomer, thus serving as a possible mechanism to quiesce the basal kinase activity of HPK1.
claims.evidence: Inferred from structural studies

claims.claim: The trans-inhibitory posture of the activation loop is disrupted when threonine residue 165 and serine residue 171 are phosphorylated.
claims.source: This trans-inhibitory posture of the activation loop is disrupted when the threonine residue 165 and serine residue 171 are phosphorylated (Johnson et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Johnson et al., 2019

claims.claim: The proteolytically cleaved 54 kD C-terminal fragment has no catalytic activity but plays an important role in the regulation of apoptosis via its ability to inhibit the NFκB pathway.
claims.source: The proteolytically cleaved 54 kD C-terminal fragment that contains three proline-rich regions and the citron homology domain has no catalytic activity, but plays an important role in the regulation of apoptosis via its ability to inhibit the NFκB pathway (Chen et al., 1999; Arnold et al., 2001).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Chen et al., 1999; Arnold et al., 2001

claims.claim: Full length HPK1 activates the NFκB pathway during the early, non-AICD-sensitive phase of T cell activation through phosphorylation of the linker region of CARMA1 at serine 549 and 551.
claims.source: Full length HPK1 had been shown to activate the NFκB pathway during the early, non-AICD-sensitive phase of T cell activation (Arnold et al., 2001; Brenner et al., 2005), through phosphorylation of the linker region of CARMA1 at serine 549 and 551 (Arnold et al., 2001; Brenner et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Arnold et al., 2001; Brenner et al., 2005; Brenner et al., 2009

claims.claim: The phosphorylated CARMA1 complexes with Bcl10 and MALT1 to form the CARMA1/Bcl10/MALT1 complex that phosphorylates and activates IKK kinase activity.
claims.source: The phosphorylated CARMA1 complexes with Bcl10 and MALT1 to form the CARMA1/Bcl10/MALT1 that phosphorylates and activates IKK kinase activity, resulting in IKK degradation and initiation of the NFκB activation cascade (Brenner et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Brenner et al., 2009

claims.claim: Once HPK1 is cleaved by caspase, its HPK1-C fragment continues to bind to IKKα and IKKβ and sequester them in the inactive form, preventing the initiation of the NFκB cascade.
claims.source: Once HPK1 is cleaved by caspase, its HPK1-C fragment continues to bind to IKKα and IKKβ and sequester them in the inactive form, preventing the initiation of the NFκB cascade (Brenner et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Brenner et al., 2005

claims.claim: NK cells isolated from catalytically inactive K46M HPK1 mutant mice possess increased cytotoxic activity in vitro against YAC-1, a NK-sensitive murine lymphoma, when compared to wild type NK cells.
claims.source: In this regard, NK cells isolated from catalytically inactive K46M HPK1 mutant mice were shown to possess increased cytotoxic activity in vitro against YAC-1, a NK-sensitive murine lymphoma, when compared to the activity of wild type NK cells (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: The loss of HPK1 kinase activity correlates with higher titers of IgG1 and IgG2b produced in response to immunization.
claims.source: While there is no direct evidence to suggest that HPK1 is involved in ADCC, there is evidence that the loss of HPK1 kinase activity correlates with higher titers of IgG1 and IgG2b produced in response to immunization (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: HPK1-/- bone marrow derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) exhibited elevated levels of CD80 and CD86 in response to LPS stimulation.
claims.source: The first evidence that HPK1 is involved in the second step of cancer-immunity cycle came when it was shown that HPK1-/- bone marrow derived dendritic cells (BMDCs) exhibited elevated levels of CD80 and CD86 in response to receiving maturation signal via LPS stimulation (Alzabin et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Alzabin et al., 2009

claims.claim: HPK1-/- BMDCs demonstrated increased levels of IL-12 production, reduced levels of IL-10 and an enhanced ability to present peptide antigen.
claims.source: These HPK1-/- BMDCs also demonstrated increased levels of IL-12 production, reduced levels of IL-10 and an enhanced ability to present peptide antigen.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of HPK1-/- BMDC properties

claims.claim: Ovalbumin immunized HPK1-/- BMDCs could elicit a greater proliferative response of adoptively transferred OTI T cells than their wild type counterpart.
claims.source: Ovalbumin immunized HPK1-/- BMDCs could elicit a greater proliferative response of adoptively transferred OTI T cells than their wild type counterpart.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: Catalytically-inactive K46M HPK1 BMDCs elicit an elevated OTI proliferative response to ovalbumin peptide in vitro.
claims.source: This finding is consistent with the report of an elevated OTI proliferative response to enhanced antigen presentation by ovalbumin peptide-pulsed catalytically-inactive K46M HPK1 BMDCs in vitro, which suggests the enhanced antigen presentation is dependent of the HPK1 kinase activity (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: HPK1-/- BMDCs were resistant to LPS-mediated activation-induced apoptosis.
claims.source: Given that the HPK1-/- BMDCs were resistant to LPS-mediated activation-induced apoptosis and HPK1-/- T cells are also resistant to PGE2-induced apoptosis (Alzabin et al., 2009; Alzabin et al., 2010)
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Alzabin et al., 2009; Alzabin et al., 2010

claims.claim: HPK1-/- T cells are resistant to PGE2-induced apoptosis.
claims.source: Given that the HPK1-/- BMDCs were resistant to LPS-mediated activation-induced apoptosis and HPK1-/- T cells are also resistant to PGE2-induced apoptosis (Alzabin et al., 2009; Alzabin et al., 2010)
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Alzabin et al., 2009; Alzabin et al., 2010

claims.claim: The ectopic expression of HPK1 in Jurkat T cells reduced TCR-induced Erk MAPK and AP-1 activation while the expression of a catalytically inactivated point mutant form of HPK1 could not.
claims.source: The initial clue that the kinase activity of HPK1 plays a role in inhibiting TCR-induced activation signal came when it was reported that the ectopic expression of HPK1 in Jurkat T cells reduced TCR-induced Erk MAPK and AP-1 activation while the expression of a catalytically inactivated point mutant form of HPK1 could not (Liou et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liou et al., 2000

claims.claim: Jurkat cells treated with Sunitinib malate (Sutent) could produce more IL-2 in response to TCR engagement, resulting in enhanced phosphorylation of Erk MAPK and elevated IL-2 production.
claims.source: This early finding is consistent with our early observation that Jurkat cells, when treated with Sunitinib malate (Sutent), could produce more IL-2 in response to TCR engagement, resulting in enhanced phosphorylation of Erk MAPK and elevated IL-2 production [unpublished observation and (Johnson et al., 2019)].
claims.evidence: Supported by unpublished observation and citation to Johnson et al., 2019

claims.claim: Sutent is a multi-kinase inhibitor capable of inhibiting HPK1 kinase activity in vitro at an IC50 of 15 nM.
claims.source: Sutent, the multi-kinase inhibitor was capable of inhibiting HPK1 kinase activity in vitro at an IC50 of 15 nM (Anastassiadis et al., 2011; Davis et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Anastassiadis et al., 2011; Davis et al., 2011

claims.claim: The loss of HPK1 correlates strongly with heightened level of T cell activation as evidenced by increased proliferation, sustained TCR-induced calcium flux and elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-2, TNF-α and IFN-γ.
claims.source: The loss of HPK1 correlates strongly with the heightened level of T cell activation as evidenced by increased proliferation, sustained TCR-induced calcium flux and elevated levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-2, TNF-α and IFN-γ (Alzabin et al., 2010; Shui et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Alzabin et al., 2010; Shui et al., 2007

claims.claim: HPK1-/- mice possess an enhanced immunopathologic response to myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) in a murine experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model.
claims.source: HPK1-/- mice also possess an enhanced immunopathologic response to myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) in a murine experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) model (Shui et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Shui et al., 2007

claims.claim: HPK1 expression was reduced in CD4+ T cells of systemic lupus erythematosus patients due to jumonji domain containing 3 (JMJD3)-mediated H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) of the HPK1 promoter.
claims.source: These murine studies were consistent with a report that HPK1 expression was reduced in CD4+ T cells of systemic lupus erythematosus patients due to jumonji domain containing 3 (JMJD3)-mediated H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) of the HPK1 promoter (Zhang et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2011

claims.claim: A reduction of HPK1 expression was detected by microarray analysis of RNA prepared from PBMC of psoriatic arthritis patients.
claims.source: A similar report of the reduction of HPK1 expression was detected by microarray analysis of RNA prepared from PBMC of psoriatic arthritis patients (Batliwalla et al., 2005; Stoeckman et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Batliwalla et al., 2005; Stoeckman et al., 2006

claims.claim: Adoptive transfer of HPK1-/- T cells is sufficient to confer host mice with the ability to reject the 3LL lung carcinoma.
claims.source: The first evidence that the loss of HPK1 has a positive impact on T cell response to cancer in vivo came when Alzabin et al. demonstrated in the Lewis lung carcinoma model that adoptive transfer of HPK1-/- T cells is sufficient to confer host mice with the ability to reject the 3LL lung carcinoma, revealing the importance of HPK1 in the control of the T cell intrinsic response to cancer antigens (Alzabin et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Alzabin et al., 2010

claims.claim: T cells from both K46E and K46M mutant mice failed to phosphorylate SLP-76 at serine 376 and responded to TCR engagement with elevated activation of the Erk MAPK pathway and higher levels of IL-2 and IFN-γ production compared to wild type T cells.
claims.source: T cells from both the K46E and K46M mutant mice failed to phosphorylate SLP-76 at serine 376 and responded to TCR engagement with elevated activation of the Erk MAPK pathway and coincided with higher levels of IL-2 and IFN-γ production when compared to wild type T cells.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results from K46E and K46M mice

claims.claim: When K46E mice were immunized with ovalbumin-anti-DEC205 conjugate, a higher percentage of OVA peptide primed SIINFEKL+ CD8 T cells expressed elevated levels of IFN-γ and granzyme B, despite the lack of a significant increase in SIINFEKL+ CD8 T cells.
claims.source: When the K46E mice were immunized with an ovalbumin-anti-DEC205 conjugate as a model antigen, targeting ovalbumin to DEC205+ dendritic cells for cross-presentation priming of CD8+ T cells, it was observed that a higher percentage of OVA peptide primed SIINFEKL+ CD8 T cells expressed elevated levels of IFN-γ- and granzyme B, despite the lack of a significant increase in SIINFEKL+ CD8 T cells (Hernandez et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Hernandez et al., 2018

claims.claim: When catalytically inactive K46M HPK1 mutant mice were immunized with ovalbumin, a higher percentage of BrdU-incorporated CD45+, CD4+, CD3+ splenic and lymph node T cells were found in the immunized K46M HPK1 mice than in the wild type cohort.
claims.source: In contrast, when catalytically inactive K46M HPK1 mutant mice were immunized with ovalbumin, a higher percentage of BrdU-incorporated CD45+, CD4+, CD3+ splenic and lymph node T cells were found in the immunized K46M HPK1 mice than in the wild type cohort (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: CX3CL1 transcripts are found to be elevated in tumor draining lymph nodes of tumor-bearing K46M HPK1 mice.
claims.source: With regard to the possible involvement of HPK1 in the regulation of T cell trafficking to the tumor, CX3CL1 transcripts are found to be elevated in tumor draining lymph nodes of tumor-bearing K46M HPK1 mice (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: High levels of CX3CL1 is known to be associated with an increased number of CD8+ and CD4+ tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in colorectal cancer and is a good prognostic indicator of survival.
claims.source: High levels of CX3CL1 is known to be associated with an increased number of CD8+ and CD4+tumor infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in colorectal cancer and is a good prognostic indicator of survival (Franciszkiewicz et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Franciszkiewicz et al., 2012

claims.claim: Increased CD4+ and CD8+ TILs were found in tumors grown in K46M mice.
claims.source: While there is no direct evidence to implicate HPK1 in CX3CL1-mediate chemotaxis, reports of increased CD4+ and CD8+ TILs in tumors grown in K46M mice and increased CD8+ TILs in tumors grown in K46E mice allow us to infer that the loss of HPK1 kinase activity might be contributing to the increased chemokine-mediated chemotaxis towards tumors (Liu et al., 2019; Hernandez et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2019; Hernandez et al., 2018

claims.claim: Increased CD8+ TILs were found in tumors grown in K46E mice.
claims.source: While there is no direct evidence to implicate HPK1 in CX3CL1-mediate chemotaxis, reports of increased CD4+ and CD8+ TILs in tumors grown in K46M mice and increased CD8+ TILs in tumors grown in K46E mice allow us to infer that the loss of HPK1 kinase activity might be contributing to the increased chemokine-mediated chemotaxis towards tumors (Liu et al., 2019; Hernandez et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2019; Hernandez et al., 2018

claims.claim: HPK1 negatively regulates the TCR-initiated LFA-1 activation by binding to the SH2 domain of SLP-76, limiting the available pool of SLP-76 to form the supramolecular complex with ADAP.
claims.source: HPK1 negatively regulates the TCR-initiated LFA-1 activation by binding to the SH2 domain of SLP-76, limiting the available pool of SLP-76 to form the supramolecular complex with ADAP (Wang et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Wang et al., 2004

claims.claim: HPK1 uses its protein scaffolding ability to compete with and to disrupt the formation of the ADAP-based LFA-1 activation complex.
claims.source: In this model, there is no evidence that HPK1 mediates its negative regulatory function via its kinase activity, but rather HPK1 uses its protein scaffolding ability to compete with and to disrupt the formation of the ADAP-based LFA-1 activation complex (Patzak et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Patzak et al., 2010

claims.claim: Translational silencing of HPK1 by shRNA resulted in an increased Rap1 activation and cell adhesion to ICAM-1.
claims.source: Translational silencing of HPK1 by shRNA resulted in an increased Rap1 activation and cell adhesion to ICAM-1 (Königsberger et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Königsberger et al., 2010

claims.claim: HPK1 functions as an essential activator of the CXCL1-induced LFA-1 activation of polymorphonuclear neutrophils, enabling neutrophils to adhere to ICAM-1-expressing cells and extravasate into tumors.
claims.source: While these studies provided evidence that HPK1 functions as negative regulator of LFA-1-dependent cellular adhesion in T and B cells, HPK1 assumes a diametrically opposed role of being an essential activator of the CXCL1-induced LFA-1 activation of polymorphonuclear neutrophils, enabling neutrophils to adhere to ICAM-1-expressing cells and extravasate into tumors (Jakob et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Jakob et al., 2013

claims.claim: K46M HPK1 mutant T cells are resistant to PGE2-mediated and adenosine-mediated inhibition of TCR-induced proliferative responses, as well as to the suppression of TCR-induced IL-2 production.
claims.source: Studies using genetically modified mice suggests that T cells that do not express HPK1 or express the catalytical inactive form of HPK1 are resistant to many of these immunosuppressive factors. These HPK1 mutant T cells have significant resistance to PGE2-mediated and adenosine-mediated inhibition of TCR-induced proliferative responses, as well as to the suppression of TCR-induced IL-2 production (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: K46M HPK1 mutant mice could effectively control the growth of a syngeneic sarcoma tumor (1956) that produces high levels of both PGE2 and adenosine.
claims.source: K46M HPK1 mutant mice could effectively control the growth of a syngeneic sarcoma tumor (1956) that produces high levels of both PGE2 and adenosine.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: Nanostring analysis of tumor draining lymph nodes from K46M mice that harbor the 1956 tumor revealed that pathways known to associate with the apoptotic network are down-regulated.
claims.source: Nanostring analysis of tumor draining lymph nodes from K46M mice that harbor the 1956 tumor revealed that pathways known to associate with the apoptotic network are down-regulated (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: HPK1-/- T cells are resistant to PGE2-mediated suppression of TCR-induced proliferative responses and IL-2 production, as well as being resistant to PGE2-mediated apoptosis.
claims.source: This collection of findings is consistent with the previous report that HPK1-/- T cells are resistant to PGE2-mediated suppression of TCR-induced proliferative responses and IL-2 production, as well as being resistant to PGE2-mediated apoptosis (Alzabin et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Alzabin et al., 2010

claims.claim: HPK1-/- mice could effectively control the growth of PGE2-dependent syngeneic lung carcinoma tumor (3LL).
claims.source: As with the K46M mice, HPK1-/- mice could effectively control the of PGE2-dependent growth of syngeneic lung carcinoma tumor (3LL), suggesting that the resistance to PGE2-mediated inhibition may contribute to effective tumor control (Alzabin et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Alzabin et al., 2010

claims.claim: K46E HPK1 mutant mice successfully control the growth of GL261 glioma.
claims.source: The catalytically inactive K46E and K46M HPK1 mutant mice successfully control the growth of GL261 glioma and sarcoma 1956, respectively (Hernandez et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Hernandez et al., 2018

claims.claim: K46M HPK1 mutant mice successfully control the growth of sarcoma 1956.
claims.source: The catalytically inactive K46E and K46M HPK1 mutant mice successfully control the growth of GL261 glioma and sarcoma 1956, respectively (Hernandez et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: K46E mice responded to GL261 tumor with increased CD8+ T cell infiltrates that express elevated levels of IFN-γ and TNF-α.
claims.source: K46E mice responded to GL261 tumor with increased CD8+ T cell infiltrates that expresses elevated levels of IFN-γ and TNF-α.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: K46E mice showed a 90% response rate in the control of GL261 tumor growth.
claims.source: This elevated anti-tumor immunity correlated with a 90% response rate in the control of tumor growth.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: Analysis of TILs in K46M mice bearing 1956 tumors revealed a significant reduction of Treg infiltrates and a corresponding increase in the CD8+ to Treg cell ratios.
claims.source: Analysis of TILs in this model revealed a significant reduction of Treg infiltrates and thus a corresponding increase in the CD8+ to Treg cell ratios.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: Quantitative PCR and nanostring analysis of RNA isolated from 1956 tumors in K46M mice revealed increased immune cell markers involved in mediating anti-tumor immunity, most notably CD4, CD8, IFN-γ, TNF-α, granzyme B, CD28, CD11c and CD11b.
claims.source: Quantitative PCR and nanostring analysis of RNA isolated from these tumors revealed increased immune cell markers involved in mediating anti-tumor immunity, most notably CD4, CD8, IFN-γ, TNF-α, granzyme B, CD28, CD11c and CD11b are elevated in K46M mice.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: K46E HPK1 mutant mice infected with Clone 13 strain of LCMV responded with reduced viral titers in blood, kidney and liver, which correspond with nearly a two fold increase in the frequency of LCMV-specific GP276+ CD8 T cells compared to wild type mice.
claims.source: To assess whether HPK1 kinase activity plays a role in regulating T cell exhaustion, the K46E HPK1 mutant mice were infected with the Clone 13 strain of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) and found to responded with reduced viral titers in blood, kidney and liver, which correspond with nearly a two fold increase compared to wild type mice in the frequency of LCMV-specific GP276+ CD8 T cells (Hernandez et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Hernandez et al., 2018

claims.claim: With the PD-1/PD-L1 axis blocked by anti-PD-L1 antibody, K46E mice cleared the LCMV virus to levels below the sensitivity of detection.
claims.source: With the PD-1/PD-L1 axis blocked by the anti-PD-L1 antibody, the K46E mice cleared the LCMV virus to levels below the sensitivity of detection, confirming that the K46E T cells were still sensitive to PD-1/PD-L1-mediated inhibition (Hernandez et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Hernandez et al., 2018

claims.claim: The inhibitory pathways regulated by HPK1 is distinct from that of PD-1.
claims.source: Thus, the inhibitory pathways regulated by HPK1 is distinct from that of PD-1, which suggests that a small molecule inhibitor of HPK1 could be used in conjunction with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the experimental results showing additive effects of HPK1 loss and PD-L1 blockade

claims.claim: The homeostatic level of HPK1-/- Tregs were elevated when compared to wild type Tregs.
claims.source: For this reason, the homeostatic level of HPK1-/- Tregs were assessed and found to be elevated when compared to the wild type Tregs (Sawasdikosol et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Sawasdikosol et al., 2020

claims.claim: HPK1-/- Tregs have reduced ability to inhibit TCR-induced proliferative responses by effector T cells.
claims.source: Further analysis revealed that HPK1-/- Tregs have reduced ability to inhibit TCR-induced proliferative responses by effector T cells.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: HPK1-/- Tregs respond to TCR engagement with an elevated and sustained Erk MAPK and p65/RelA NF-κB phosphorylation, which correlate with their ability to produce IFN-γ, CCL3, CCL4 and IL-2.
claims.source: In addition, HPK1-/- Tregs respond to TCR engagement with an elevated and sustained Erk MAPK and p65/RelA NF-κB phosphorylation, which correlate with their ability to produce IFN-γ, CCL3, CCL4 and IL-2.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: K46M HPK1 mutant mice bearing 1956 tumors possess a lower percentage of Treg relative to CD45+ TILs, causing an increase in the CD8+ effector T cells:Tregs ratio.
claims.source: While the functional properties of K46M HPK1 mutant Tregs have not been characterized, the K46M HPK1 mutant mice bearing the 1956 tumors possess a lower percentage of Treg relative to CD45+ TILs, causing an increase in the CD8+ effector T cells:Tregs ratio (Liu et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019

claims.claim: There have been no published report of enhanced anti-tumor immunity that have been elicited by small molecule inhibitor of HPK1 to date.
claims.source: While a large number of HPK1 programs have identified lead HPK1 kinase inhibitors that can block HPK1 kinase activity with the half maximal inhibitory concentration IC50 values in the low nM concentration, there have been no published report of enhanced anti-tumor immunity that have been elicit by small molecule inhibitor of HPK1 to date.
claims.evidence: Based on knowledge of the current state of HPK1 inhibitor development

claims.claim: It is extremely challenging to develop a highly selective small molecule that does not inhibit one or more of the closely related Ste20 family member of HPK1.
claims.source: Given that there are quite a number of Ste20 family members that function as MAP4Ks and share high sequence homology of their kinase domains with HPK1, it is extremely challenging to develop a highly selective small molecule that does not inhibit one or more of the closely related Ste20 family member of HPK1.
claims.evidence: Based on knowledge of kinase inhibitor development challenges

claims.claim: HPK1-/- mice appeared to reject 3LL tumors far more effectively than the catalytically inactive HPK1 mutant mice could reject other syngeneic tumors.
claims.source: The fact that HPK1-/- mice appeared to reject 3LL tumors far more effectively than the catalytically inactive HPK1 mutant mice could reject other syngeneic tumors supports the possibility that a complete removal of HPK1 protein is required for the maximal anti-tumor immunity outcome.
claims.evidence: Inferred from comparison of experimental results across different studies

claims.claim: HPK1 transcripts are found in all embryonic tissues.
claims.source: Given that HPK1 transcripts are found is all embryonic tissues, it may not be surprising that transcripts have been found in non-hematopoietic cell lineages, including brain and testes (Kiefer et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Kiefer et al., 1996

claims.claim: HPK1 transcripts have been found in non-hematopoietic cell lineages, including brain and testes.
claims.source: Given that HPK1 transcripts are found is all embryonic tissues, it may not be surprising that transcripts have been found in non-hematopoietic cell lineages, including brain and testes (Kiefer et al., 1996).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Kiefer et al., 1996

claims.claim: HPK1 has been shown to be expressed and associated with the oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase, AXL in early pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PanIN).
claims.source: Recently, HPK1 has also been shown to be expressed and associated with the oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase, AXL in early pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PanIN) (Wang et al., 2009; Song et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Wang et al., 2009; Song et al., 2020

claims.claim: As PanIN progresses to more aggressive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAC), HPK1 expression is lost via CUL7/Fbxw8 ubiquitin ligase-dependent targeting of HPK1 for degradation via the 26 s proteasome.
claims.source: As PanIN progresses to a more aggressive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDAC), HPK1 expression is loss via CUL7/Fbxw8 ubiquitin ligase-dependent targeting of HPK1 for degradation via the 26 s proteasome (Wang et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Wang et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2014

claims.claim: The presence of HPK1 promotes the increased association between AXL and the c-Cbl ubiquitin ligase, and the increased association between these two molecules correlates with AXL ubiquitination and downregulation.
claims.source: The presence of HPK1 promotes the increased association between AXL and the c-Cbl ubiquitin ligase, and the increased association between these two molecules correlates with AXL ubiquitination and downregulation.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of HPK1's role in PanIN cells

claims.claim: Reconstituting HPK1 expression in PDAC cells causes PDAC cells to undergo cell cycle arrest and growth inhibition.
claims.source: Reconstituting HPK1 expression in PDAC cells causes PDAC cells to undergo cell cycle arrest and growth inhibition.
claims.evidence: Inferred from the description of experimental results

claims.claim: HPK1 may be functioning as a tumor suppressor gene in PanIN cells.
claims.source: These results suggest that HPK1 may be functioning as a tumor suppressor gene in PanIN cells.
claims.evidence: Speculated based on the experimental observations

claims.claim: There is no known human disease linked directly to a mutation or deletion of the HPK1 locus.
claims.source: While the interest in HPK1 rests on solid genetic evidence obtained from murine tumor models, a note of caution is warranted in that, to date, there is no known human disease linked directly to a mutation or deletion of the HPK1 locus.

claims.source: Correlations between reduced HPK1 expression levels and autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (Zhang et al., 2011) and psoriatic arthritis (Zhou et al., 1999) have been reported
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2011 and Zhou et al., 1999

claims.claim: There is no direct evidence to suggest that individuals with reduced HPK1 expression have enhanced anti-tumor immune responses.
claims.source: Correlations between reduced HPK1 expression levels and autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (Zhang et al., 2011) and psoriatic arthritis (Zhou et al., 1999) have been reported, but there is no direct evidence to suggest that these individuals have enhanced anti-tumor immune responses due to decreased HPK1 protein levels.
claims.evidence: Based on the absence of evidence in the literature

results.result: Current immune checkpoint inhibitor therapies show variable efficacy across tumor types (15-87% response rates), highlighting the need for biomarker development and expansion of therapeutic targets beyond existing checkpoints.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C4 are well-supported by citations to peer-reviewed literature (Ribas and Wolchok, 2018; Chen and Mellman, 2017; Havel et al., 2019). The response rate variability and need for additional therapeutic approaches are established facts in the immuno-oncology field.

results.result: Small molecule kinase inhibitors represent a viable alternative approach for immuno-oncology drug development, leveraging mature screening technologies, though selecting appropriate targets among >500 human kinases remains challenging.
results.evaluation: Claims C5-C8 are supported by citations and established knowledge of pharmaceutical development. The existence of mature screening platforms and the challenge of target selection among numerous kinases are well-documented aspects of kinase inhibitor development.

results.result: HPK1 (MAP4K1) is a hematopoietic cell-restricted serine/threonine kinase that functions as a negative regulator of TCR-mediated T cell activation signals.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C11 are well-supported by multiple citations (Chen and Mellman, 2013; Kiefer et al., 1996; Hu et al., 1996; Liou et al., 2000). The characterization of HPK1 as a negative regulator of TCR signaling is established in the literature.

results.result: HPK1 is catalytically activated by multiple cell surface receptors on hematopoietic cells, including TCR, BCR, Fas, EPOR, TGFβR, EP2R/EP4R, and LPS receptors.
results.evaluation: Claims C12-C18 are supported by multiple citations documenting HPK1 activation by various receptors. The evidence spans multiple independent studies, though C18 includes speculation about TLR2/TLR4 involvement that is appropriately qualified.

results.result: Upon TCR engagement, HPK1 is recruited to lipid rafts via LAT/Gads interactions, phosphorylated by ZAP-70, and achieves full catalytic activity through autophosphorylation and PKD-mediated phosphorylation. Active HPK1 phosphorylates SLP-76 and Gads, creating 14-3-3 binding sites that destabilize the LAT signalosome and lead to SLP-76 degradation.
results.evaluation: Claims C19-C26 describe a detailed mechanistic pathway supported by multiple citations (Liou et al., 2000; Ling et al., 2001; Sauer et al., 2001; Arnold et al., 2005; Di Bartolo et al., 2007; Lasserre et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2012a). The sequential steps are well-documented, though some claims (C20, C23, C26) are inferred from the cited work rather than explicitly stated.

results.result: HPK1 negatively regulates BCR-induced B cell activation through a mechanism similar to TCR regulation, involving Syk/Lyn-mediated activation and BLNK phosphorylation leading to BLNK degradation.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C30 are supported by citations and experimental data from HPK1-/- B cells (Wang et al., 2012b; Sauer et al., 2001; Tsuji et al., 2001). The elevated signaling responses in knockout cells provide strong evidence for HPK1's negative regulatory role.

results.result: PGE2, produced by COX-2-overexpressing tumors, activates HPK1 through EP2/EP4 receptors via a PKA-dependent mechanism distinct from TCR-mediated activation, contributing to tumor-mediated immune suppression.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C38 are supported by multiple citations (Sawasdikosol et al., 2003, 2007; Vercammen and Ceuppens, 1987; Wang and DuBois, 2008; Greenhough et al., 2009). The experimental evidence from mutant Jurkat cells (C37) provides strong support for the distinct activation mechanism (C38).

results.result: Fas engagement triggers caspase-mediated cleavage of HPK1 at D385, generating a hyperactive N-terminal kinase domain that activates JNK via MEKK1/MKK/JNK cascade. Structural studies reveal HPK1 exists as a domain-swapped dimer with trans-inhibitory regulation disrupted by phosphorylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C39-C46 are supported by multiple citations (Dickens et al., 2012; Chen et al., 1999; Arnold et al., 2007; Kiefer et al., 1996; Hu et al., 1996; Chen and Tan, 2000; Wu et al., 2019; Johnson et al., 2019). The structural and functional characterization is well-documented, though C45 involves inference from structural data.

results.result: The caspase-cleaved C-terminal fragment of HPK1 regulates apoptosis by inhibiting NFκB signaling. Full-length HPK1 activates NFκB via CARMA1 phosphorylation during early T cell activation, but the cleaved C-terminal fragment sequesters IKKα/β to prevent NFκB activation during AICD.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C50 are supported by multiple citations (Chen et al., 1999; Arnold et al., 2001; Brenner et al., 2005, 2009). The dual role of HPK1 in NFκB regulation depending on its cleavage state is well-documented and mechanistically coherent.

results.result: NK cells from catalytically inactive K46M HPK1 mice show increased cytotoxic activity against YAC-1 lymphoma in vitro, and loss of HPK1 kinase activity correlates with higher antibody titers upon immunization.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C52 are supported by experimental data from Liu et al., 2019. However, the connection to ADCC (C52) is speculative as acknowledged in the text. The in vitro NK cytotoxicity data is direct evidence, but in vivo relevance requires validation.

results.result: HPK1-/- and K46M HPK1 dendritic cells show enhanced maturation markers (CD80/CD86), altered cytokine production (increased IL-12, decreased IL-10), enhanced antigen presentation capacity, and resistance to activation-induced apoptosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C58 are supported by experimental data from multiple studies (Alzabin et al., 2009, 2010; Liu et al., 2019). The convergent evidence from both knockout and kinase-dead mutants strengthens the conclusion that HPK1 kinase activity negatively regulates dendritic cell function.

results.result: Loss of HPK1 or its kinase activity enhances T cell activation, as demonstrated by ectopic expression studies, pharmacological inhibition with Sutent, and genetic ablation studies. HPK1-/- mice show enhanced autoimmune responses in EAE models, and reduced HPK1 expression is associated with human autoimmune diseases.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C65 are supported by multiple citations and experimental data (Liou et al., 2000; Johnson et al., 2019; Anastassiadis et al., 2011; Alzabin et al., 2010; Shui et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2011; Batliwalla et al., 2005). However, C60 includes unpublished observations which weakens that specific claim. The convergent evidence from multiple approaches supports the overall conclusion.

results.result: Adoptive transfer of HPK1-/- T cells confers tumor rejection ability in 3LL lung carcinoma model. Catalytically inactive K46E and K46M HPK1 mutant T cells show enhanced activation with elevated cytokine production and altered proliferative responses to immunization.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C69 are supported by experimental data from multiple studies (Alzabin et al., 2010; Hernandez et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2019). The apparent discrepancy between K46E (no proliferative advantage) and K46M (increased proliferation) is acknowledged in the text and requires further investigation, but doesn't invalidate the overall finding of enhanced activation.

results.result: Loss of HPK1 kinase activity correlates with elevated CX3CL1 expression in tumor-draining lymph nodes and increased CD4+ and CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in K46M and K46E mice.
results.evaluation: Claims C70-C73 are supported by citations (Liu et al., 2019; Hernandez et al., 2018; Franciszkiewicz et al., 2012), but the manuscript explicitly states there is no direct evidence linking HPK1 to CX3CL1-mediated chemotaxis. The correlation is observed but the mechanistic connection remains speculative.

results.result: HPK1 negatively regulates LFA-1-mediated T cell adhesion through protein scaffolding interactions with SLP-76 that compete with ADAP complex formation, though HPK1 plays an opposite activating role in neutrophil LFA-1 activation.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C77 are supported by citations (Wang et al., 2004; Patzak et al., 2010; Königsberger et al., 2010; Jakob et al., 2013). However, the manuscript notes that kinase activity involvement hasn't been tested using K46M/K46E mutants, leaving uncertainty about whether this is purely a scaffolding function.

results.result: K46M and HPK1-/- T cells are resistant to PGE2 and adenosine-mediated suppression of TCR responses and apoptosis. These mice effectively control growth of immunosuppressive tumors (1956 sarcoma, 3LL lung carcinoma) with downregulated apoptotic pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C82 are supported by experimental data from multiple studies (Liu et al., 2019; Alzabin et al., 2010). The convergent evidence from both knockout and kinase-dead mutants across different tumor models provides strong support for HPK1's role in mediating tumor-induced immunosuppression.

results.result: Catalytically inactive K46E and K46M HPK1 mice successfully control GL261 glioma and 1956 sarcoma growth, respectively, with increased CD8+ TIL infiltration, elevated effector cytokines, reduced Treg infiltration, and increased CD8+:Treg ratios.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C88 are supported by experimental data from Hernandez et al., 2018 and Liu et al., 2019. The tumor control phenotype is well-documented with multiple supporting immune parameters (TIL composition, cytokine production, immune markers). The 90% response rate in K46E mice is a strong quantitative outcome.

results.result: K46E HPK1 mice show enhanced control of chronic LCMV infection with increased virus-specific CD8+ T cells. Combined anti-PD-L1 treatment results in complete viral clearance, demonstrating that HPK1 and PD-1 regulate distinct inhibitory pathways.
results.evaluation: Claims C89-C91 are supported by experimental data from Hernandez et al., 2018. The additive effect of HPK1 loss and PD-L1 blockade provides strong evidence for distinct mechanisms. This has important therapeutic implications for combination therapy, though C91 involves inference from the experimental results.

results.result: HPK1-/- Tregs show elevated homeostatic levels, reduced suppressive function, enhanced activation signaling (Erk MAPK, NFκB), and production of atypical cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2, CCL3, CCL4). K46M tumor-bearing mice show reduced Treg infiltration and increased CD8+:Treg ratios.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C95 are supported by experimental data from Sawasdikosol et al., 2020 and Liu et al., 2019. The 'fragile' Treg phenotype in HPK1-/- mice is well-characterized. However, the functional properties of K46M Tregs remain uncharacterized, limiting conclusions about kinase-dependent effects.

results.result: Despite numerous HPK1 inhibitor programs achieving low nM IC50 values, no published reports demonstrate enhanced anti-tumor immunity from small molecule HPK1 inhibitors. Developing selective inhibitors is challenging due to high sequence homology among Ste20 family MAP4Ks.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C97 are based on knowledge of the current state of drug development. The absence of published efficacy data despite multiple programs is a notable gap. The selectivity challenge is a well-known issue in kinase inhibitor development, particularly for closely related family members.

results.result: HPK1-/- mice appear to reject 3LL tumors more effectively than catalytically inactive HPK1 mutants reject other syngeneic tumors, suggesting complete protein removal may be required for maximal anti-tumor immunity.
results.evaluation: Claim C98 involves cross-study comparison of different tumor models (3LL vs. GL261/1956) which may have inherent differences in immunogenicity. The inference that complete protein removal is superior requires direct comparison in the same tumor model with appropriate controls.

results.result: HPK1 is expressed in embryonic tissues and some non-hematopoietic lineages (brain, testes). In pancreatic cancer, HPK1 is expressed in early PanIN lesions where it promotes AXL downregulation, but is lost during progression to PDAC via CUL7/Fbxw8-mediated degradation. HPK1 reconstitution causes PDAC growth inhibition, suggesting a tumor suppressor role.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C105 are supported by citations (Kiefer et al., 1996; Wang et al., 2009, 2014; Song et al., 2020). The tumor suppressor role (C105) is appropriately qualified as speculative. This raises important safety considerations for HPK1-targeted therapies in patients with PanIN lesions.

results.result: No human disease is directly linked to HPK1 mutations or deletions. Correlations exist between reduced HPK1 expression and autoimmune diseases (SLE, psoriatic arthritis), but no evidence links reduced HPK1 to enhanced anti-tumor immunity in humans.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C108 are based on knowledge of human genetics and supported by citations (Zhang et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 1999). The absence of human genetic evidence is an important limitation for translating murine findings to clinical applications, appropriately highlighted as a cautionary note.
